confidence_notes: Food and drink anchors rest on three web searches: the RBA rate and two price searches. The first price search returned cost-of-living aggregators (crowdsourced, some from 2023). Those gave a beer of about €3, a cappuccino of about €2, an inexpensive meal of about €15–17 and a mid-range meal for two of about $60 in 2023 terms. I adjusted these upward for 2026 inflation and for San Sebastián's tourist premium. The second search found no reliable current price for beer, wine or cocktails. Cocktail and wine anchors are therefore based on the usual local relationship to beer: a cocktail at about 3x and a wine glass at about 1.2x. Accommodation anchors are holistic model estimates, not checked against any booking pages or listings. They assume July peak-season pricing, when San Sebastián is expensive and varies widely. Accommodation is the least certain group. USD figures assume EUR/USD of roughly 1.17, which I did not look up.
comparable_city_reasoning: San Sebastián is a high-demand Basque coastal destination. Restaurant and accommodation prices are above the Spanish average and closer to Bilbao or the pricier parts of Barcelona, while café and bar drink prices stay modest. Beer and coffee prices are typical of northern Spain.
